title: Fixed Deposits: Tax on FD Interest & Key Rules for Depositors
description: Interest earned on Fixed Deposits (FDs) is fully taxable as 'Income from Other Sources' and added to your total income. This interest is taxed according to yo.

faq.a: Yes, interest earned on Fixed Deposits is fully taxable. It is added to your total annual income and taxed according to your applicable income tax slab rate.

faq.q: What is the TDS threshold for FD interest?
faq.a: For individuals below 60 years, the TDS threshold is ₹40,000 annually per bank. For senior citizens (60 years and above), this limit is ₹50,000 annually per bank.

faq.q: Can I avoid TDS on FD interest?
faq.a: Yes, if your total income for the financial year is below the basic exemption limit, you can submit Form 15G (for non-senior citizens) or Form 15H (for senior citizens) to your bank to avoid TDS deduction.

faq.q: Is interest from tax-saving FDs also taxable?
faq.a: Yes, while the principal amount invested in a 5-year tax-saving FD qualifies for deduction under Section 80C, the interest earned on it is fully taxable as per your income tax slab.

faq.q: How is interest from cumulative FDs taxed?
faq.a: For cumulative FDs, the interest is taxable on an accrual basis each financial year, even if you receive the entire amount only at maturity. You must declare the accrued interest annually in your Income Tax Return.

faq.q: What happens if I don't provide PAN to the bank for my FD?
faq.a: If you do not provide your PAN to the bank, TDS on your FD interest will be deducted at a higher rate of 20%, instead of the standard 10%, once the interest crosses the threshold.
